## 固定收益市場主線

10月16日美國公債走勢依天期分歧。科技股再度遭到拋售，支撐短天期債券；油價上漲，加上市場對政府減少長債供給的期待落空，則壓抑長天期公債。2年期殖利率下降2.99個基點至4.7083%，10年期反而上升1.48個基點至5.0728%。布蘭特原油上漲3.72%至每桶$109.86，讓本週大多時間圍繞AI融資疑慮交易的市場，再次面對眼前的通膨壓力。

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh在曼谷的談話降低了10月升息預期，但未排除繼續緊縮。隨後公布的進口物價漲幅與工業生產增幅均高於預期，凸顯成本壓力與經濟活動仍強。紐約時間中午，財政部公布的交易商問卷未能直接釋出部分投資人期待的長天期發行縮減訊號。殖利率曲線轉陡，部分扭轉本週偏好長債的走勢，即使那斯達克100指數又下跌2.50%也未改變這項分歧。

信用市場對借款人的選擇更為嚴格。美國投資級利差小幅擴大，高收益與硬通貨新興市場債券利差則明顯擴大。美國銀行仍將發債規模擴大至$80億，與房貸證券化延後、較年輕AI企業融資日益困難形成對照。殖利率具有吸引力，並不等於能持續取得新資金；實際交易已呈現這項差別，而不只是證券價格下跌。

## 油價與美債供給打斷債市反彈

週五亞洲與歐洲股市回升，削弱了推動週四美債大漲的避險需求，長天期公債開盤承壓。Bloomberg盤中報導指出，10至30年期殖利率一度上升逾5個基點。美股上午9時30分開盤後，科技股再度下跌，美債跌幅收斂，短天期殖利率也回吐先前漲幅。

接近中午時行情再次轉向。美國指標原油突破每桶$100，財政部同時公布11月4日季度再融資前的主要交易商調查題目。投資人原先期待問卷明確討論縮減長債標售，甚至停止發行20年期公債；財政部實際上只是廣泛詢問，面對需求結構變化及其未來演變，應考慮哪些標售規模調整。

RBC Capital Markets的Blake Gwinn認為，這種措辭令期待強烈訊號的投資人失望。問卷公布後，30年期美債相對同天期利率交換走弱。道明證券策略師Molly Brooks表示，公司預期長天期標售規模最快也要到2月才會改變，與押注下一個再融資季度即會縮減的部位不同。實際籌資決策仍待後續公布，週四部分買盤所期待的供給減輕尚未獲得確認。

收盤曲線呈現這項分歧：5年期殖利率下降0.92個基點至4.8683%，30年期上升1.53個基點至5.4209%；2年與10年期利差擴大4.47個基點至36.45個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大4.52個基點至71.26個基點。長債本週仍保有可觀漲幅，10年與30年期殖利率分別下降16.5與17.47個基點，2年期則下降7.86個基點。不過，10年期殖利率較一個月前仍高6.98個基點。

週五10年期名目殖利率上升，來自通膨補償增加：實質殖利率下降0.63個基點至2.722%，損益兩平通膨率卻上升2.11個基點至2.3508%。本週名目殖利率的降幅，幾乎全由實質殖利率下降16.31個基點貢獻，損益兩平通膨率僅下降0.19個基點。因此，當日反轉是通膨重新定價，而不是扣除通膨後的借款成本全面上升。

Warsh在美國交易時段前重申維持物價穩定的承諾，提及9月撤除寬鬆措施，但不願預判今年剩餘會議的決定。Bloomberg報導，談話後市場隱含的10月升息機率由約27%降至15%以下；週五稍晚交易時回到約20%，年底前再升息25個基點仍已完全反映於定價。

他對AI的說明也為政策辯論提供重要條件：中期可望帶來正面供給效果，但在效益實現前，AI已先增加總需求，對就業的影響則不確定。Jan Hatzius率領的高盛經濟學家認為，談話指向10月暫停、12月最後一次升息。美國銀行Michael Hartnett在10月15日研究報告中持不同看法，預期10月就會升息，以恢復抗通膨公信力。雙方分歧在於何時緊縮，而非當前通膨問題是否已消失。

週五的新數據顯示物價與產出均強於預期。9月進口物價月增1.1%，高於市場預期0.8%，前值修正為上升0.5%；出口物價上升2.2%，高於預期1%，前值修正為上升1.2%。工業生產月增0.7%，高於預期0.4%，前月增幅上修至0.1%。金融市場質疑投資成長能否持續之際，全國生產仍較預期強勁。

能源成本的傳導也有新進展。9月卡車貨運生產者物價年增逾19%，機票價格上漲約22%。塗料與塗層生產商RPM International執行長Frank Sullivan表示，地緣政治事件迫使公司追加春季未規劃的漲價。儘管他形容需求依舊低迷，公司會計年度第一季已以漲價全額抵銷通膨增加的成本，預期第二季也能做到。

食品價格走勢並不一致。食品雜貨消費者物價微降，但9月食品生產者物價上升1.2%，配製動物飼料價格月增2.3%、年增6.6%。Santander的Stephen Stanley預期，更多壓力最終會轉嫁給消費者。花旗經濟學家Veronica Clark則指出，家具與家電價格仍持平或下跌，尚未見到能源帶動的廣泛商品通膨。她預期每月CPI將相對溫和，薪資成長疲弱與勞動市場降溫也會限制企業轉嫁供給衝擊的能力。

油價仍加重眼前壓力。WTI收在$101.41，單日上漲3.51%、全週上漲10.41%；布蘭特原油週五上漲後，全週漲幅達4.91%。涉及胡塞武裝與沙烏地阿拉伯的攻擊、俄羅斯與烏克蘭能源設施再度互遭襲擊，以及市場對擬議增加俄羅斯柴油供應的疑慮，使實體供給風險持續受到關注。標普500下跌1.09%，半導體股下跌3.83%，VIX上升21.45%至19.99。與週四不同，股市再跌未能帶動各天期美債全面上漲。

財政數據也限制了供給減輕的樂觀預期。2026會計年度聯邦赤字達$1.99兆，較前一年的$1.78兆高約12%。支出增加約6%至$7.4兆，快於收入增加3%至$5.4兆；淨利息支出增加$814億，創下$1.05兆新高。單看9月，赤字為$270億，略低於市場預期$290億，也遠低於8月的$1,670億。

全年個人所得稅收入增加$1,890億，但2025年稅法延長減稅並新增扣除額後，企業稅收入減少逾$700億。社會安全支出增加$864億至$1.67兆，Medicare支出增加$760億至$1.07兆。這些數字顯示，借款需求同時來自經常性計畫支出與利息負擔，並非只取決於單月籌資安排。

週末分析進一步量化利息支出的敏感度。9月底可交易美債平均付息率達3.52%，五年前僅1.47%。道明證券估算，整條曲線上升100個基點，將使2027年利息成本增加$3,100億。策略師Gennadiy Goldberg也指出一項抵銷因素：第二季名目GDP年增6.3%，仍高於美債殖利率。布魯金斯研究院經濟學家Louise Sheiner認為，財政能力正逐步受侵蝕，但標售需求仍穩健，尚非迫在眉睫的籌資危機。

週五公布的8月國際資本流動（TIC）長期淨流入達$2,792億，遠高於預期$752億，並扭轉7月淨流出$279億。這項歷史跨境資金流入數據，與擴大的全年赤字同時呈現較強的需求，但未解決財政部未來應如何配置發債天期的問題。

## AI融資壓力延伸至新增借款

CoreWeave週五股價下跌約12%，回吐週四由供應商支持帶動的反彈，全週跌幅約25%。那斯達克100全週下跌5.49%，半導體股跌11.41%。新一波賣壓讓市場疑慮由既有AI投資價格，延伸到下一批專案取得資金的條件。

Bloomberg週末信用市場報導引述高盛研究指出，高收益資料中心債券平均價格接近95美元，低於6月的101美元。Tract Capital Management、Prime Data Centers與Cipher Digital開發的債務融資工具，本週均跌至發行以來最低價。MetLife Investment Management的John Yovanovic認為，預期供給已成為重新定價的關鍵：未來一年半還有大量借款，投資人可以等待後續提供更高報酬的交易，不必急於承接目前的證券。

高盛統計，今年美元投資級與高收益專案融資發行已達$1,060億，接近2025全年$370億的三倍；策略師預期明年全球發行將超過$3,000億。同份研究認為，資金成本提高會讓部分投資減速，而非使投資全面中斷。剛結束的一週高收益發行已相當稀少，僅三筆交易，合計$20億。

新融資的定價更為困難。摩根大通與高盛週四為AI雲端新創Volta Infrastructure Holdings的$50億槓桿貸款加碼條件，最終殖利率高於最初討論的11%。Shorecliff Asset Management的Grant Nachman表示，以目前價格，大型無擔保新型雲端業者融資可能成本高到難以負擔、買盤不足，或兩者兼有。他預期，新融資將需要資產或已簽約現金流作為擔保，以及更強的債權人保護；可轉換債、股權與證券化都是替代方案。

債權人要求保護的營運原因，在於建設支出與可產生收入的運算服務之間存在時間落差。GMI Cloud執行長Alex Yeh指出，業者在專案仍陸續上線時就得償債。公司上月向14家銀行取得新台幣139億元、約合$4.29億的五年期貸款，用於台灣資料中心，利率約3.45%；另正為泰國尋求$3億融資。他將這筆本幣貸款與CoreWeave殖利率約15%的債券相比，並認為亞洲供應鏈與在地融資是自身優勢；這項比較也涉及不同幣別及融資結構。

Cathie Wood週五在首爾提出較樂觀的看法。她表示，ARK Investment Management在跌勢中增持CoreWeave與Cerebras，認為年輕公司隨市場發展，可能靠成長度過借款昂貴的階段，並以Coinbase債券過去受壓為例。她也指出，高記憶體晶片價格正在傷害消費裝置需求，難以持續，意味著目前支撐部分半導體獲利的零組件漲價潮也面臨限制。

週末，Nscale出現具體營運挫折。這家英國新型雲端業者證實，微軟退出位於英格蘭艾塞克斯郡Loughton的擬議資料中心合作。該場址曾面臨電力限制，但Nscale未說明微軟退出的具體原因。公司表示仍將推進專案，正尋找替代電源，與微軟的其他合約則不受影響。其IPO申報資料顯示，微軟與Anthropic約占公司合約的85%。

Nscale此時正尋求透過IPO籌資最多$30億，其挪威旗艦中心已延後六個月，目前運轉容量僅6.4百萬瓦，原定為30百萬瓦。這些發展發生於週五債市收盤後，使接下來的籌資挑戰更為嚴峻：若約定容量未如期到位，客戶合約就無法產生預期現金流。

本週美債反彈也涉及相關供給因素。Natixis利率策略師John Briggs在週末評估中指出，AI相關債務虧損可能降低投資人承接新債的意願，減輕長天期美債面對的資金競爭。Bloomberg另報導，商品交易顧問解除大規模偏空期貨部位，也助長本週漲勢。瑞士寶盛的Afonso Borges認為，AI帶動的潛在衰退會是傳統負向需求衝擊，有助通膨降溫；Standard Bank的Steven Barrow則懷疑，在仍可能升息且能源通膨未退之際，債券能否持續發揮這種作用。週五科技股再跌、長債殖利率卻上升，正呈現了這項分歧。

## 銀行發債需求穩健，其他借款人調整籌資方向

美國銀行週五募得$80億，高於最初行銷的至少$60億，顯示市場對大型成熟借款人發行的債券仍有需求。四批債券天期介於3至11年，最長一批規模$27.5億，以較美債高95個基點定價，較初步討論收窄約25個基點。

今年此前僅四筆週五發債、合計$27億，因此這是一筆罕見的大型週五交易。在假期縮短的交易週，美國銀行、摩根大通與摩根士丹利合計發行$180億，整體投資級發行達$285億，接近交易商預期。這是美國銀行4月以來首次發債，全年借款因此達$250億；該行第三季未發行，為財報後籌資留下較大空間。

Kimberly-Clark則開始與投資人通話，評估由摩根大通安排、可能分五批發行的2至10年期債券。這筆潛在借款與尚待完成的Kenvue收購有關，目前交易估值約$360億，其中現金對價$67億；摩根大通已提供$77億過橋融資。收購預計年底前完成，Kimberly-Clark將於11月5日公布財報，此時接洽投資人，可望在慣常的財報前發債暫停期之前，替換收購融資。

房貸借款人的發行則不順。Figure延後原定週四定價的$3.46億住宅房貸證券化，資產池含4,101筆貸款，最長期限30年；最大一批為AAA級、規模$2.563億，報價利差約155個基點。Figure表示，直接出售整筆貸款的結果更好。房地美也延後逾$4.4億公寓房貸債券，Bridge Investment Group則擱置$11.9億商用不動產CLO。

Sound Inpatient Physicians轉向私募市場，接近與包括Monarch Alternative Capital及PGIM在內的既有貸款人完成$10億再融資，先前6月的聯貸嘗試未果。擬議交易將債務延長五年，利率為基準加6個百分點，預計隔週完成。公司2024年重整後，息稅折舊攤銷前獲利已倍增至逾$2.5億，但殖利率上升仍促使其改變重返聯貸市場的計畫。

軟體業收購融資仍可取得。Thoma Bravo支持的Proofpoint已為約$63億的Varonis收購取得$12.5億融資，摩根大通與瑞銀將主導後續高收益債發行，收購預計2027上半年完成。Thoma Bravo將投入股權資金，安大略省教師退休基金也將投資Proofpoint。此前Proofpoint於7月展延$43億既有債務，為此提供多項貸款人保護；仍有$7.35億於2028年到期。

歐洲方面，Partners Group採取核准貸款人限制，使問題貸款更難退出。在約€60億債務接近再融資之際，該公司已阻止機會型投資人買入Emeria、Ammega與Breitling等公司的債務或取得資料。Emeria於2028年3月到期的貸款報價約為面額70%，Ammega於2028年12月到期者為79%，Breitling於2028年10月到期者為82%。Emeria正協商€36億債務，可能需要股東投入現金。

這些限制可保護既有貸款人，避免重整手法使其債權順位被壓低，卻也減少CLO及其他持有人欲出售時的買家。Emeria債券不受核准貸款人名單限制；貸款即使透過間接參貸轉讓也可能困難，因文件允許檢視最終經濟曝險，部分情況下甚至可取消交易。再融資協商升溫之際，價格下跌凸顯了這項流動性限制。

印度Yes Bank判決帶來相反的估值難題。最高法院週四推翻2020年AT1減記後，Kotak Mahindra與Nippon Life暫停受影響債券基金或退休基金的新申購，評估目前帳面列為零的持債應如何定價。Franklin Templeton表示，隔離持有的59億盧比資產將維持零估值至實際回收，再分配所得。判決涉及原先841.5億盧比減記；持債可能大幅重估，但估值仍待確定，基金業者先暫停新增申購。

土耳其基金危機也正傳導至企業籌資。贖回違約後，業界投資組合已縮減1.5兆里拉；該國公司債市場超過1兆里拉，共同基金持有約三分之一。Gedik Yatirim新分析指出，監管機關已清算基金的投資組合中，58.6%、約3,340億里拉屬不具流動性的資產。週四監管機關以當前不確定性為由，移除Tera Yatirim Menkul連同增資提出的690億里拉發債申請。Perform Portfoy的Altan Aydin預期，小型借款人受創最深，大型發行人仍可取得市場融資。

美國貨幣市場則是供給承接問題，而非普遍缺現金。財政部10月上半月淨發行近$1,000億國庫券，巴克萊預期隨後六週將超過$3,200億。國庫券利率相對SOFR交換利率的利差擴大，但10月大部分時間SOFR仍在準備金利率或以下。貨幣基金將存續期間縮短至35.3天；交易商擴大資產負債表，加上槓桿相對價值交易的融資需求減少，協助附買回市場維持穩定。聯準會連續第三個月未為準備金管理買入國庫券，即使隔夜融資平靜，民間買家仍須承接更多供給。

## 央行權衡能源通膨與市場緊縮效果

歐洲央行管理委員會成員Olli Rehn週五提出審慎調整步調的理由：12月預測將提供更多成長與通膨資訊，目前第二輪效應及價格壓力擴散仍有限，較高債券殖利率已壓抑經濟活動、產生通膨降溫效果。但他也提醒，不能因此假定金融條件已使央行不必再採取政策行動，薪資與勞動市場同樣需要考量。

德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel另表示，若情況持續，仍可能進一步行動。他將殖利率上升歸因於能源成本、成長韌性，以及對利率相對不敏感的新AI借款人，並否認歐洲正步入另一場金融危機。兩人的側重不同：市場緊縮使政策步調需要謹慎，但通膨持續也讓再次升息仍在考慮之列。

法國為這項平衡帶來政治考驗。國會正審議€430億減赤措施，財長Roland Lescure表示，高殖利率有助說服各黨維持財政紀律。他對最終通過有信心，但承認可能動用繞過國會的憲法程序，包括有導致政府倒台風險的第49.3條。歐洲穩定機制主管Pierre Gramegna則表示，利差仍受控制，救助基金遠未到需要介入的程度。

週末抗議加劇財政調整的難度。針對公共服務與生活成本的示威演變成搶劫與縱火，商店及公共建築受損，據報逾2,000人被捕。馬克宏要求恢復秩序，並安排週一召開危機會議。這些週五債市收盤後發生的事件，增加了預算協商的國內壓力。

Christine Lagarde週六聲明呼籲採取暫時、精準的能源援助，債務高的國家則應整頓財政。她認為成長風險偏向下行、通膨風險偏向上行；能源衝擊大到不能忽略，但貨幣政策仍宜審慎回應。這也凸顯抑制通膨與避免財政應對措施長期增加借款之間的實際衝突。

英國央行總裁Andrew Bailey週五表示，物價與薪資第二輪效應的跡象仍溫和，同時承認經濟韌性強於預期。英國此時正考慮將銀行公司稅附加稅率由3%調回接近原先8%的水準；Bloomberg Intelligence估算，完全恢復可增加約£30億收入。借款成本升高，已讓財政大臣John Healey接手時£236億的財政緩衝縮水約一半。Bailey未對當前提案表態，但先前曾警告，對銀行報酬課稅可能提高房貸成本、減少存款利息並妨礙資本形成。

日本央行總裁植田和男週五對基礎通膨措辭轉強，表示不能容忍其進一步超出2%。他指出金融條件仍寬鬆，是否再升息取決於物價與經濟活動，中東、AI需求與匯率則影響時機。IMF的Rahul Anand另預期還會升息一次，由目前1.25%走向約1.5%的中性利率中心估值；較廣的估計區間為1.1%至2.2%。

日本國內買家投入現金仍謹慎。富國生命一般帳戶資產約6%放在現金與存款，高於歷來2%至3%。因選擇不為到期次順位債再融資、可投資資金減少，公司將全年日本公債增持計畫由¥1,100億降至¥800億。其日圓債策略未變，除非殖利率大幅超出預測區間，否則預期從外國債券進一步移轉的規模將維持溫和。

散戶對公司債的需求則較強。樂天發行創紀錄¥4,000億的5.5年期債券，票息4.37%，其中¥3,600億售予個人、¥400億售予機構。機構批次相對指標10年期日本公債的利差，由初步行銷170至180個基點擴大至200個基點，最終需求約為該批次1.3倍。2026年日本散戶公司債發行約達¥3.2兆，比去年紀錄高逾15%。家庭參與踴躍，機構投資人卻要求更大的發行讓利。

澳洲週五標售也顯示買家對殖利率的反應：A$10億、2029年4月到期公債的需求接近發行量五倍，投標倍數為2018年10月以來最高。週末房市數據顯示，各首府城市共舉行1,423場拍賣，較前週少18.6%、較去年同期少約46%；成交率由48.8%升至51.2%。不過，墨爾本新實施的底價揭露規定也影響活動，不能只用利率解釋。

## 印尼信心衝擊與主權籌資選擇

MSCI以可投資性問題為由，提議將印尼股票由新興市場直接移至獨立市場、不經邊境市場類別，造成一場獨立的信心衝擊。雅加達指標股指下跌11.6%，創1998年1月以來最大跌幅，交易暫停30分鐘；印尼盾貶值，政府公債也下跌，市場治理因此直接進入貨幣政策討論。

花旗經濟學家Helmi Arman將10月21日決策預測由不變改為升息50個基點至6.25%，認為可防止股票資金外流蔓延到債券與本國投資組合。華僑銀行經濟學家則把可能升息25個基點的時點由12月提前。Bank Permata的Josua Pardede仍預期本月維持5.75%，主張以匯市干預及其他穩定措施因應；但若外流持續、匯率疲弱及通膨壓力出現，之後可能升息。

影響不只在眼前賣壓。高盛估算，在極端降至邊境市場的情境下，被動資金外流可能達$130億；Pardede則在重新分類的另一情境下估計，外資股票賣出可能為$30億至$50億，取決於先前已出清多少。PT Bank Danamon的Irman Faiz警告，取得新增外資的能力減弱，可能推升政府風險溢價與企業融資成本。所有權透明度、自由流通股揭露及執法，將是預計2027年中前決策的核心。

中國則以不同方式吸引資金。潘功勝承諾推動人民幣債券規則更接近國際標準，並爭取主要結算機構接受其作為擔保品。當局也希望在香港更頻繁發行主權債、建立更完整的離岸天期結構，並開放衍生工具與債券期貨參與。目標是將成本較低的人民幣融資，與國際投資人可持有、可避險的工具銜接。

安哥拉正將這個市場納入籌資多元化考量。國庫官員Ottoniel dos Santos表示，繼武士債之後，熊貓債與伊斯蘭債券都是選項，今年不再規劃其他國際發行。2026年已發行$40億歐洲債券，其中支持$12億負債管理，減輕2028至2029年的償付壓力。實現油價平均每桶$87，高於預算$61，使剩餘融資需求降至$2億至$4億。Dos Santos否認正協商展延中國貸款期限，表示籌資選擇將待2027年預算完成後決定。

玻利維亞則一面準備交易，一面等待低於5月重返國際市場時9.75%殖利率的融資成本。財長Christian Andres Morales表示，官員正與德意志銀行及Santander更新文件。可能的負債管理操作涉及公共退休金管理機構Gestora Publica持有的約$9億，屬2028及2030年到期合計約$15億債務的一部分。擬議操作與IMF計畫、燃料補貼改革並行，光第四季燃料進口預計就需$6億至$8億。

塞內加爾預算草案為債務談判提出新的財政承諾。2027年赤字目標為GDP的4.7%，低於今年修正後7.6%，也低於IMF於4月預測的5.7%。支出將減少2.9%至7.4兆非洲金融共同體法郎，收入增加2.8%至6兆；初級赤字由4,500億縮至477億非洲金融共同體法郎，相當於GDP的0.2%。花旗指出，削減資本支出與加強控管是調整主力。國會時程、未完成的審計及債權人協商，仍使期待11月取得IMF董事會批准的進程更複雜。

IMF對阿根廷的籌資評估則轉強。區域副主管Luis Cubeddu表示，當局已具備良好條件應付2027年義務，理由包括買入逾$150億外匯存底，以及展延披索債務，使接近一半義務延至選舉後，遠高於今年稍早15%。經濟部長Luis Caputo正洽談進入2027年前至少$20億多邊融資，並與世界銀行討論約$100億民間部門專案資金。若國際發債成本相對既有替代方案具有競爭力，他會考慮發行。

儘管第二季經濟萎縮、7月表現疲弱，Caputo仍預測建設與房貸將帶動復甦，並駁斥衰退預期。他聲稱銀行逾放正在下降，但官方數據尚未呈現。對經濟活動的分歧，和能否取得多邊貸款一樣影響籌資前景：世界銀行預期，將在有選舉及逾$250億債務到期的一年協助流動性需求。

巴西當前信用數據則為選舉行情提供較審慎的背景。Serasa Experian統計，8月有創紀錄930萬家企業逾期，欠款合計2,440億雷亞爾；金融體系逾放率達5%。魯拉提議免除微型創業者126億雷亞爾債務，Flavio Bolsonaro則主張設立由石油拍賣與資產出售收入支持的再融資基金。兩名候選人都支持福利承諾，使迅速抑制支出更困難。Chimera Capital的Rafael Nogueira預期，即使利率快速下降，過度舉債的後遺症仍將至少延續兩年。

## 後續市場觀察

接下來的美國房市數據，將檢驗高融資成本對AI建設以外領域的抑制程度。10月19日公布10月NAHB指數，市場預期由32降至31。10月20日的9月新屋開工預期由127.5萬戶升至130萬戶，營建許可初值則預期由140.3萬戶降至140萬戶；成屋待完成銷售預期月增率持平，前值為上升0.3%。同日還有ADP每週就業變動，隨後週三公布MBA房貸申請、週四公布首次申領失業救濟金人數。聯準會進入談話靜默期，這些數據將承擔更多眼前政策討論的資訊角色。

週五的10月製造業與服務業PMI初值、密西根大學消費者信心終值，將延續成長檢驗。AI相關財報則另行檢視投資週期：特斯拉與Meta週三公布，微軟及亞馬遜分別於10月28、29日公布。對已向較不成熟基礎設施借款人要求更高報酬的債權人而言，營收、支出承諾與專案落實情況都很重要。交易商預期下週美國投資級發行約$250億，繼美國銀行成功發債後，初級市場將再受考驗。

財政部10月21日續發20年期公債，10月22日標售5年期抗通膨公債（TIPS），都在11月4日再融資決策之前。國庫券標售也持續進行，近期供給負擔正在增加。週五問卷內容廣泛，未決的核心仍是財政部會在本次再融資調整長天期發行組合，還是留待之後季度；抗通膨債需求同時面對油價重新上漲的壓力。

中國週一公布GDP與經濟活動數據，將顯示工業強勢是否傳至內需。Bloomberg經濟學家調查預期，第三季GDP年增4.4%，前季為4.3%，仍低於全年4.5%至5%的目標區間。9月工業生產預期年增5.4%，前值5.2%；零售銷售僅預期增0.5%，前值0.4%；前九個月固定資產投資則預期下降7.3%。金融街論壇週一開幕，投資人評估近期財政與融資支持效果之際，也可從中觀察新的政策訊號。

英國週二勞動數據與週三通膨數據，將協助釐清11月5日英國央行決策前，政策是否需要急於行動的分歧。經濟學家預期9月年通膨率由3.1%升至3.4%；Bloomberg Economics預期，截至8月的三個月失業率由4.9%升至5%。日本週五CPI預期整體及排除生鮮食品的通膨率均為2.1%，排除生鮮食品與能源者為2.3%。這些實際物價讀數將與植田對基礎通膨轉強的措辭相互參照。

印尼週三決策，將直接面對MSCI提案引發的匯率信心考驗。同日南非公布通膨與中期預算，可觀察總裁Lesetja Kganyago所稱的財政及貨幣紀律是否仍按軌道推進。法國週五將迎來穆迪評等審查，背景包括預算協商與週末動亂。巴西月中通膨將在10月25日決選前公布；民間信用困境使最終財政方案比競選承諾本身更重要。

能源仍是各項決策之外的獨立風險。週一亞洲早盤、台北時間07:00以前，布蘭特原油在週五大漲後回落，美股期貨小幅回升。澤倫斯基週末提出，以增加愛國者飛彈換取停止攻擊俄羅斯煉油廠，為外交進程增添一項有條件的提議；荷姆茲海峽至黑海的供應干擾仍在。燃料供給能否改善，以及AI企業能否把承諾化為營運收入，是決定本週政府公債反彈還能延伸多遠的兩項不同因素。

overall_summary.headline: 短天期美債上漲，油價與供給期待落空推升長債殖利率
overall_summary.session_narrative:
週五美債依天期分歧收盤：2年期殖利率下降2.99個基點至4.7083%，10年期則上升1.48個基點至5.0728%。科技股再遭拋售支撐短債，但布蘭特原油上漲3.72%至$109.86，加上財政部交易商問卷令市場失望，壓抑長天期公債。問卷未在11月4日再融資決策前，明確釋出縮減長天期標售的訊號。2年與10年期利差擴大4.47個基點至36.45個基點。

10年期名目殖利率上升來自通膨補償增加：損益兩平通膨率上升2.11個基點至2.3508%，實質殖利率則下降0.63個基點至2.722%。長債全週仍保有可觀漲幅。Kevin Warsh的談話降低10月聯準會升息預期，但未排除進一步緊縮；9月進口物價與工業生產也雙雙高於預期。

那斯達克100下跌2.50%，AI融資疑慮由資產價格下跌延伸到新增借款條件。Volta Infrastructure的$50億槓桿貸款須加碼條件，殖利率高於最初討論的11%。美國投資級信用利差小幅擴大，高收益與硬通貨新興市場利差明顯擴大。然而，美國銀行將發債規模擴大至$80億，與房貸證券化延後形成對照，顯示其他發行人調整籌資計畫之際，成熟借款人仍能取得資金。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasury trading split by maturity on October 16 as renewed selling in technology shares supported short-dated debt, while rising oil prices and disappointment over prospective cuts to government bond supply weighed on the long end. The two-year yield fell 2.99 basis points to 4.7083%, but the 10-year rose 1.48 basis points to 5.0728%. Brent gained 3.72% to $109.86 a barrel, restoring an immediate inflation concern to a market that had spent much of the week responding to anxiety over artificial-intelligence financing.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's Bangkok appearance reduced expectations for an October increase without closing the door to further tightening. Stronger-than-expected import prices and industrial production then underscored the continuing pressure from costs and activity. By midday in New York, Treasury's dealer questionnaire had failed to provide the direct signal of lower long-maturity issuance some investors wanted. The curve steepened, partially reversing the week's preference for longer bonds, even as the Nasdaq 100 lost another 2.50%.

Credit conditions became more selective. U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly, while high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened noticeably. Bank of America nevertheless raised $8 billion in an enlarged offering, contrasting with mortgage securitizations being postponed and increasing difficulty financing younger AI companies. The distinction between an attractive yield and reliable access to new capital was becoming visible in actual transactions, not just in falling security prices.

## Oil and Treasury Supply Interrupt the Bond Recovery

Long Treasuries began Friday under pressure as Asian and European shares recovered, reducing the demand for safety that had driven Thursday's sharp rally. Bloomberg's intraday account put increases in 10- to 30-year yields above 5 basis points at one stage. Those losses diminished when U.S. technology shares resumed falling after the 9:30 a.m. equity opening, and short-dated yields erased their earlier increases.

The next reversal came around midday. U.S. benchmark crude moved above $100 a barrel while Treasury published the questions for its primary-dealer survey ahead of the November 4 quarterly refunding. Investors had entertained the possibility of an explicit discussion of smaller long-end auctions, including an end to 20-year issuance. Instead, Treasury asked broadly what future auction-size changes should be considered in light of structural changes in demand and expectations for its evolution.

RBC Capital Markets' Blake Gwinn regarded the wording as a disappointment for investors expecting a strong signal. Thirty-year Treasuries cheapened against comparable interest-rate swaps after the release. TD Securities strategist Molly Brooks said her firm did not expect long-end auction sizes to change before February at the earliest, in contrast with positions anticipating a reduction in the coming refunding quarter. The questionnaire left the actual financing decision ahead, rather than delivering the supply relief embedded in some of Thursday's buying.

The closing curve captured that division. Five-year yields fell 0.92 basis point to 4.8683%, while the 30-year rose 1.53 basis points to 5.4209%. The 2s10s spread widened 4.47 basis points to 36.45, and 2s30s increased 4.52 to 71.26. Longer debt still retained substantial weekly gains: 10-year yields were down 16.5 basis points and 30-year yields down 17.47, compared with a 7.86-basis-point decline at two years. Over the month, however, the 10-year remained 6.98 basis points higher.

Inflation compensation accounted for Friday's increase in the nominal 10-year yield. Its real yield declined 0.63 basis point to 2.722%, but the breakeven rose 2.11 basis points to 2.3508%. Over the week, almost all the nominal rally came from a 16.31-basis-point drop in real yields, with breakevens down only 0.19 basis point. The daily reversal therefore reflected renewed inflation pricing rather than an across-the-board increase in inflation-adjusted borrowing costs.

Warsh's appearance had preceded the U.S. session. He reiterated the commitment to price stability, referred to September's removal of accommodation and declined to prejudge the remaining meetings of the year. Bloomberg reported that the market-implied probability of an October increase fell below 15% immediately after his remarks from about 27% beforehand. Later Friday trading put that probability around 20%, while another quarter-point increase by year-end remained fully priced.

His discussion of AI supplied a substantive condition behind the policy debate. Warsh expects a positive supply effect over the medium term, but said the technology is increasing aggregate demand before those benefits arrive, with uncertain employment consequences. Goldman Sachs economists led by Jan Hatzius interpreted the communication as pointing toward an October pause and a final increase in December. Bank of America's Michael Hartnett offered a different view in an October 15 research note, expecting an October increase to restore inflation credibility. That disagreement concerned the timing of restraint, not whether the current inflation problem had disappeared.

Friday's fresh releases gave policymakers stronger readings on both prices and output. September import prices increased 1.1% month on month, exceeding the 0.8% consensus and following a revised 0.5% rise. Export prices climbed 2.2%, against 1% expected and a revised 1.2% previous increase. Industrial production rose 0.7%, versus a 0.4% consensus, after an upwardly revised 0.1% gain. National production thus strengthened more than expected even while financial markets questioned the durability of investment growth.

New reporting on the transmission of energy costs added detail to the inflation debate. Truck-freight producer prices were more than 19% above a year earlier in September, and airfares were up about 22%. RPM International chief executive Frank Sullivan said geopolitical events had forced additional price increases that the paint and coatings producer had not planned in the spring. The company covered inflation dollar for dollar in its fiscal first quarter and expected to do so again in the second, despite demand that Sullivan described as still subdued.

Food presented a less uniform picture. Grocery consumer prices had edged lower, but producer food prices increased 1.2% in September, while prepared animal-feed prices rose 2.3% on the month and 6.6% over the year. Santander's Stephen Stanley expects more of that pressure eventually to reach consumers. Citi economist Veronica Clark countered that furniture and appliance prices remained flat or falling and that broad energy-driven goods inflation was not evident. She expects relatively benign monthly CPI readings alongside muted wages and a cooler labor market, limiting businesses' ability to pass through supply shocks.

Oil nevertheless intensified the immediate pressure. WTI finished at $101.41, up 3.51% on the day and 10.41% over the week. Brent's Friday advance took its weekly gain to 4.91%. Attacks involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, renewed exchanges against Russian and Ukrainian energy infrastructure, and doubts over the proposed release of more Russian diesel kept physical supply risks prominent. The S&P 500 lost 1.09%, semiconductor shares fell 3.83%, and the VIX rose 21.45% to 19.99. Unlike Thursday, renewed equity losses did not carry the whole Treasury curve higher.

The fiscal release supplied another current constraint on supply optimism. The federal deficit reached $1.99 trillion in fiscal 2026, about 12% above the previous year's $1.78 trillion. Spending increased roughly 6% to $7.4 trillion, outpacing a 3% rise in receipts to $5.4 trillion. Net interest expense increased $81.4 billion to a record $1.05 trillion. September alone recorded a $27 billion shortfall, slightly smaller than the $29 billion consensus and much smaller than August's $167 billion gap.

The annual accounts also showed individual-tax revenue rising $189 billion while corporate-tax receipts fell more than $70 billion after the 2025 tax legislation extended cuts and introduced deductions. Social Security outlays increased $86.4 billion to $1.67 trillion, and Medicare rose $76 billion to $1.07 trillion. Those figures locate the borrowing requirement in both recurring program spending and the interest bill, rather than in a single month's financing choices.

A weekend analysis quantified the sensitivity of that bill. The average rate paid on marketable Treasuries reached 3.52% at September's end, compared with 1.47% five years earlier. TD Securities calculated that a 100-basis-point rise across the curve would add $310 billion to 2027 interest costs. Its strategist Gennadiy Goldberg also identified an offset: nominal GDP growth of 6.3% year on year in Q2 remained above Treasury yields. Brookings economist Louise Sheiner described a gradual erosion of fiscal capacity rather than an immediate financing crisis, with auction demand still solid.

August net long-term Treasury International Capital flows, released Friday, were $279.2 billion, well above the $75.2 billion consensus and reversing July's $27.9 billion outflow. That historical cross-border inflow arrived alongside the larger annual deficit, providing a stronger demand observation without resolving the future maturity mix Treasury must finance.

## AI Financing Stress Reaches New Borrowing

CoreWeave shares fell about 12% Friday, undoing Thursday's supplier-backed recovery and leaving the stock down roughly 25% for the week. The Nasdaq 100's weekly loss reached 5.49%, while semiconductor shares fell 11.41%. The fresh selling extended concern from the price of existing AI investments toward the terms on which the next projects could raise money.

Bloomberg's weekend credit account showed high-yield data-center bonds averaging nearly $95, compared with $101 in June, citing Goldman Sachs research. Debt financing facilities developed by Tract Capital Management, Prime Data Centers and Cipher Digital fell to their lowest prices since issuance during the week. MetLife Investment Management's John Yovanovic argued that prospective supply was now central to the repricing: investors faced another year and a half of borrowing and could wait rather than accept securities likely to be followed by more expensive deals.

Goldman's figures put U.S. dollar high-grade and high-yield project-finance issuance at $106 billion this year, almost triple the $37 billion raised in all of 2025. Its strategists see worldwide issuance exceeding $300 billion next year. The same research expects higher capital costs to slow some investment rather than derail it altogether. High-yield issuance was already sparse during the completed week, with only three deals totaling $2 billion.

Execution was becoming harder. JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs sweetened terms Thursday on a $5 billion leveraged-loan sale for AI cloud startup Volta Infrastructure Holdings. The eventual yield exceeded the 11% initially discussed. Shorecliff Asset Management's Grant Nachman said a large unsecured neocloud offering at current prices would probably be prohibitively expensive, fail to attract sufficient buyers, or both. He expects new financings to require assets or contracted cash flows as security and stronger creditor protections, with convertible debt, equity and securitization among the alternatives.

The operational reason for those protections is the gap between construction spending and usable computing revenue. GMI Cloud chief executive Alex Yeh said operators must service debt while projects are still being brought online. His company secured a NT$13.9 billion, or $429 million, five-year loan from 14 banks last month for a Taiwanese data center, at roughly 3.45%, and has been seeking another $300 million for Thailand. Yeh contrasted that local-currency loan with CoreWeave bonds yielding around 15%. The different currencies and financing structures are part of the comparison: Asian supply-chain access and local funding are advantages he sees for his own business.

Cathie Wood supplied a fresh, more optimistic assessment in Seoul Friday. ARK Investment Management added CoreWeave and Cerebras shares during the declines, she said, arguing that young companies can outgrow periods of expensive borrowing as their markets develop. She compared the episode with earlier pressure on Coinbase's bonds. Wood also said high memory-chip prices were hurting demand for consumer devices and were unlikely to persist, introducing a separate limit to the input-price boom supporting some semiconductor profits.

The weekend brought a specific operating setback at Nscale. Microsoft withdrew from a planned data-center deal in Loughton, Essex, the British neocloud confirmed. The site had faced power constraints; Nscale did not give a specific reason for Microsoft's withdrawal. The company said it remained committed to the project, was exploring alternative power sources and regarded its other Microsoft contracts as unaffected. Microsoft and Anthropic account for around 85% of Nscale's contracts, according to its IPO filing.

That withdrawal came as Nscale sought to raise as much as $3 billion in an IPO. Its flagship Norwegian center was six months late, with 6.4 megawatts operating against an intended 30 megawatts. These developments occurred after Friday's bond close and deepen the coming financing test: a customer contract cannot produce the expected cash flow if the contracted capacity is not available on schedule.

The weekly Treasury recovery had a related supply dimension. In a weekend assessment, Natixis rates strategist John Briggs said losses on AI-linked debt could reduce investors' appetite for new issues, easing competition for the Treasury long end. Commodity trading advisers exiting heavily bearish futures positions also helped the week's gains, Bloomberg reported. Julius Baer's Afonso Borges sees a potential AI-led downturn as a conventional negative-demand shock that would encourage disinflation. Standard Bank's Steven Barrow remains skeptical that bonds can sustain that role while further rate increases and energy inflation remain in prospect. Friday's rise in long yields, despite renewed technology selling, gave that disagreement a concrete market setting.

## Bank Issuance Holds Up as Other Borrowers Change Course

Bank of America demonstrated continuing demand for a large established borrower by raising $8 billion Friday, above the at-least-$6 billion transaction initially marketed. Its four-part sale spans maturities from three to 11 years. The longest tranche, a $2.75 billion bond, priced at 95 basis points over Treasuries after tightening about 25 basis points from initial discussions.

It was an unusually large Friday transaction in a year when only four prior Friday offerings had raised a combined $2.7 billion. Bank of America, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley together sold $18 billion during the holiday-shortened week; total high-grade issuance reached $28.5 billion, nearly meeting dealer expectations. Bank of America's first sale since April lifted its annual borrowing to $25 billion. The lender had sat out Q3 issuance, leaving it more room to borrow after results.

Kimberly-Clark began investor calls for a possible five-tranche offering with maturities from two to 10 years, arranged by JPMorgan. The potential borrowing is tied to its pending Kenvue acquisition, currently valued around $36 billion, including $6.7 billion in cash consideration. JPMorgan provided a $7.7 billion bridge facility. With completion expected by year-end and Kimberly-Clark's results due November 5, the calls create an opportunity to replace acquisition financing before the usual pre-earnings issuance pause.

Mortgage borrowers faced weaker execution. Figure postponed a $346 million residential mortgage-backed offering that had been intended to price Thursday. The pool comprised 4,101 loans with maturities up to 30 years; its largest tranche, rated AAA and totaling $256.3 million, was offered at a spread around 155 basis points. Figure said a whole-loan sale offered a better outcome. Freddie Mac had also delayed more than $440 million of apartment-mortgage bonds, while Bridge Investment Group shelved a $1.19 billion commercial-real-estate CLO.

Sound Inpatient Physicians was moving toward a different market altogether. It was close to a $1 billion private refinancing with existing lenders including Monarch Alternative Capital and PGIM, following an unsuccessful syndicated-loan effort in June. The proposed transaction would extend debt by five years and pay a margin of 6 percentage points above the benchmark, with closing expected the following week. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization had doubled to more than $250 million after its 2024 restructuring. Higher yields nevertheless helped change plans for a renewed syndicated sale.

Acquisition finance remained possible in software. Thoma Bravo-backed Proofpoint secured $1.25 billion of financing for its roughly $6.3 billion Varonis purchase. JPMorgan and UBS will lead a later high-yield sale, with the acquisition expected to close in H1 2027. Thoma Bravo is providing equity and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan will invest in Proofpoint. The new commitment follows Proofpoint's July extension of $4.3 billion of existing debt, which required numerous lender protections; $735 million remained due in 2028.

In Europe, Partners Group's use of approved-lender restrictions was constraining exits from troubled loans. It has blocked opportunistic investors from buying debt or accessing information at companies including Emeria, Ammega and Breitling as roughly EUR6 billion approaches refinancing. Emeria's March 2028 loan was marked around 70 cents, Ammega's December 2028 loan at 79 and Breitling's October 2028 loan at 82. Emeria is negotiating its EUR3.6 billion debt burden, with a sponsor cash contribution likely necessary.

The restrictions can protect incumbent lenders against restructuring tactics that subordinate their claims, but they also reduce the pool of buyers when CLOs and other holders want to sell. Emeria bonds are outside the approved-lender list. Even indirect loan participation can be difficult because documentation permits scrutiny of ultimate economic exposure and, in some cases, cancellation of a trade. The current price declines expose that liquidity constraint as refinancing talks intensify.

India's Yes Bank judgment produced the opposite valuation problem. Following Thursday's Supreme Court reversal of the 2020 AT1 writedown, Kotak Mahindra and Nippon Life halted subscriptions into affected debt or retirement funds while assessing how to value holdings currently marked at zero. Franklin Templeton said its segregated holdings worth 5.9 billion rupees would remain at zero until recovery, with proceeds distributed once realized. The ruling concerns the original 84.15 billion-rupee writedown. The new fund restrictions prevent fresh subscriptions while a potentially large revaluation remains unresolved.

Turkey's fund crisis was also feeding into corporate financing. Industry portfolios had shrunk by 1.5 trillion liras following redemption defaults, against a corporate-bond market exceeding 1 trillion liras in which mutual funds hold about a third. A new Gedik Yatirim analysis found that illiquid assets represented 58.6%, or roughly 334 billion liras, of portfolios in funds regulators had unwound. On Thursday, regulators removed Tera Yatirim Menkul's application for 69 billion liras of debt issuance alongside a capital increase, citing prevailing uncertainty. Perform Portfoy's Altan Aydin expects smaller borrowers to suffer most, while larger issuers retain market access.

U.S. money markets showed a separate absorption problem rather than a generalized cash shortage. Treasury issued nearly $100 billion of net bills in the first half of October, and Barclays expects more than $320 billion over the following six weeks. Bill rates widened against SOFR swaps, yet SOFR traded at or below interest on reserve balances for most of October. Money funds shortened duration to 35.3 days, while dealer balance-sheet expansion and less demand for leveraged relative-value financing helped keep repo stable. The Fed's third consecutive month without reserve-management bill purchases leaves private buyers facing more supply even as overnight funding remains calm.

## Central Banks Balance Energy Inflation Against Market Restraint

ECB Governing Council member Olli Rehn offered a fresh argument for a measured pace Friday. December's forecasts would provide more information on growth and inflation, he said, while second-round effects and broadening price pressure remained limited. Higher bond yields were already restraining activity and exerting a disinflationary influence. Rehn nevertheless cautioned against assuming those financial conditions removed the need for another policy move, pointing also to wages and the labor market.

Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel separately said further action remained possible if conditions persisted. He attributed higher yields to energy costs, resilient growth and new AI borrowers that were relatively insensitive to interest rates, while rejecting the idea that Europe was entering another financial crisis. The different emphasis matters: market restraint was a reason for caution over pace, while continuing inflation left another increase in view.

France supplied a current political test of that balance. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said high yields were helping persuade parties of the need for discipline as parliament debated EUR43 billion of deficit-reduction measures. He expressed confidence in eventual passage but acknowledged the possibility of using constitutional procedures to bypass parliament, including article 49.3 with its risk of bringing down the government. European Stability Mechanism head Pierre Gramegna said spreads remained contained and the rescue fund was far from needing to intervene.

Over the weekend, protests sharpened the difficulty of delivering that adjustment. Demonstrations over public services and living costs descended into looting and fires, with more than 2,000 arrests reported and damage to shops and public buildings. Macron called for order to be restored and scheduled a Monday crisis meeting. These later developments add domestic pressure to the budget negotiations without explaining Friday's completed bond trading.

Christine Lagarde's Saturday statement urged temporary, targeted energy relief and fiscal consolidation where debt is high. She described growth risks as tilted down and inflation risks up, with the energy shock too large to disregard but a measured monetary response appropriate. Her comments reinforced the practical tension between containing inflation and avoiding a fiscal response that adds lasting borrowing.

In Britain, Andrew Bailey said Friday that evidence of second-round price and wage effects remained subdued. He also acknowledged greater-than-expected economic resilience. His assessment came alongside a possible rise in the bank corporation-tax surcharge from 3% back toward its former 8%; a full reversal would raise about GBP3 billion, Bloomberg Intelligence estimates. Higher borrowing costs have roughly halved the GBP23.6 billion fiscal buffer inherited by Chancellor John Healey. Bailey declined to take a position on the current proposal, while his earlier warnings stressed that taxing bank returns could raise mortgage costs, reduce deposit payments and impair capital formation.

Japan's Kazuo Ueda used firmer language on underlying inflation Friday, saying he could not tolerate it moving further above 2%. Financial conditions remained accommodative, he said, and further policy increases would depend on prices and activity, with the Middle East, AI demand and exchange rates influencing timing. The IMF's Rahul Anand independently expects one more increase toward a central neutral estimate around 1.5%, within a broader 1.1%-2.2% range, against the current 1.25% policy rate.

Domestic buyers were still cautious about committing cash. Fukoku Mutual Life holds about 6% of general-account assets in cash and deposits, compared with a historical 2%-3%. It reduced its planned annual JGB accumulation to JPY80 billion from JPY110 billion because it chose not to refinance maturing subordinated debt, reducing investable funds. Its yen-bond strategy remains unchanged, with further transfers from foreign bonds expected to be moderate unless yields rise substantially beyond its forecast range.

Retail buyers provided stronger corporate demand. Rakuten sold a record JPY400 billion of 5.5-year bonds at a 4.37% coupon, with JPY360 billion going to individuals and JPY40 billion to institutions. The institutional spread widened from initial marketing at 170-180 basis points to 200 basis points over the benchmark 10-year JGB, with final demand around 1.3 times the tranche. Japanese retail corporate issuance reached about JPY3.2 trillion for 2026, more than 15% above last year's record. Strong household participation coexisted with a larger institutional concession.

Australia's Friday auction likewise showed buyers responding to yields: demand approached five times the A$1 billion of April 2029 notes offered, the strongest bid-to-cover since October 2018. Weekend housing figures showed 1,423 capital-city auctions, down 18.6% from the previous week and about 46% below a year earlier. The clearance rate improved to 51.2% from 48.8%, but Melbourne's new reserve-price disclosure rules also affected activity, complicating a purely interest-rate explanation.

## Indonesia's Shock and Sovereign Funding Choices

Indonesia suffered a distinct confidence shock when MSCI proposed moving its equities from emerging-market to standalone status, bypassing the frontier category because of investability problems. The Jakarta benchmark fell 11.6%, its largest decline since January 1998, and trading stopped for 30 minutes. The rupiah weakened and government bonds declined, bringing market governance directly into the monetary-policy debate.

Citigroup economist Helmi Arman changed his October 21 forecast from a hold to a 50-basis-point increase to 6.25%, arguing that action could prevent equity outflows spreading into bonds and domestic portfolios. OCBC economists brought forward the possibility of a 25-basis-point increase from December. Bank Permata's Josua Pardede still expects the 5.75% rate to hold this month, favoring currency intervention and other stabilization measures, but sees sustained outflows, currency weakness and inflation as conditions for a later increase.

The uncertainty extends beyond immediate selling. Goldman Sachs estimated up to $13 billion of passive outflows under an extreme frontier-downgrade scenario; Pardede sees $3 billion-$5 billion of foreign stock sales if reclassification occurs, dependent on previous liquidation. Those are different scenarios, not additive estimates. PT Bank Danamon's Irman Faiz warned that weaker access to new foreign capital could raise government risk premiums and corporate funding costs. Ownership transparency, free-float disclosure and enforcement are central to the decision expected by mid-2027.

China was pursuing a different route to attracting capital. Pan Gongsheng promised closer alignment of yuan-bond rules with international standards and efforts to secure their acceptance as collateral at major clearing houses. Authorities are also seeking more frequent sovereign issuance in Hong Kong and a fuller offshore tenor structure, alongside derivatives and bond-futures access. The policies aim to connect cheaper yuan funding with instruments international investors can hold and hedge.

Angola is considering that market as part of funding diversification. Treasury official Ottoniel dos Santos said panda bonds and sukuk are options after a Samurai issue, with no further international sale planned this year. Its $4 billion of eurobond borrowing in 2026 supported $1.2 billion of liability management, easing 2028-29 repayments. Average realized oil prices of $87 a barrel, against $61 budgeted, reduced remaining financing needs to $200 million-$400 million. Dos Santos denied negotiations to extend Chinese loan maturities and said funding choices would follow completion of the 2027 budget.

Bolivia, by contrast, is preparing a transaction while waiting for cheaper rates than the 9.75% yield it paid on its May return to international markets. Finance Minister Christian Andres Morales said officials were updating documentation with Deutsche Bank and Santander. A possible liability-management operation concerns about $900 million held by public pension administrator Gestora Publica, part of roughly $1.5 billion maturing in 2028 and 2030. The proposed operation accompanies an IMF program and fuel-subsidy reform, while Q4 fuel imports alone are expected to cost $600 million-$800 million.

Senegal's draft budget offered a new fiscal commitment in its debt negotiations. It targets a 2027 deficit of 4.7% of GDP, down from a revised 7.6% this year and below the IMF's April forecast of 5.7%. Spending would fall 2.9% to CFA7.4 trillion and revenue rise 2.8% to CFA6 trillion, with the primary deficit shrinking to CFA47.7 billion, or 0.2% of GDP, from CFA450 billion. Citi said lower capital spending and tighter controls drive much of the adjustment. Parliamentary timing, the unfinished audit and creditor negotiations still complicate the hoped-for November IMF board approval.

Argentina received a stronger financing assessment from the IMF. Deputy regional director Luis Cubeddu said the authorities were well placed to meet 2027 obligations, citing more than $15 billion of reserve purchases and peso-maturity extensions that pushed almost half of obligations beyond the election, compared with 15% earlier this year. Economy Minister Luis Caputo is discussing at least $2 billion of multilateral funding heading into 2027 and roughly $10 billion with the World Bank for private-sector projects. He would consider international issuance if its cost became competitive with existing alternatives.

Caputo also forecast a construction- and mortgage-led recovery and dismissed recession expectations, despite the Q2 contraction and July weakness. His claim that banks were seeing falling delinquencies had yet to appear in official figures. That disagreement over activity matters to the financing outlook as much as the availability of multilateral loans: the World Bank expects to support liquidity needs during a year with elections and more than $25 billion of maturities.

Brazil's current credit figures provided a sobering backdrop to its election rally. A record 9.3 million companies were delinquent in August, with overdue debt totaling 244 billion reais, according to Serasa Experian; financial-system delinquencies reached 5%. Lula proposed forgiving 12.6 billion reais owed by micro-entrepreneurs, while Flavio Bolsonaro proposed a refinancing fund backed by oil-auction and asset-sale proceeds. Both candidates support benefit commitments that complicate rapid spending restraint. Chimera Capital's Rafael Nogueira expects the leverage hangover to persist for at least another two years even if interest rates fall quickly.

## Forward Market Significance

The coming U.S. housing releases will test how much restraint high financing costs are imposing outside the AI buildout. October's NAHB index is due October 19, with consensus at 31 after 32. September housing starts on October 20 are expected at 1.30 million after 1.275 million, while preliminary permits are expected at 1.40 million after 1.403 million. Pending home sales are expected to be flat month on month after a 0.3% rise. Weekly ADP employment change arrives the same day, followed by MBA applications Wednesday and initial claims Thursday. With the Fed in its communications blackout, these releases will carry more of the immediate policy debate.

Friday's preliminary October manufacturing and services PMIs and final Michigan sentiment reading extend the growth test. AI-related earnings supply a separate assessment of the investment cycle: Tesla and Meta report Wednesday, followed by Microsoft October 28 and Amazon October 29. Revenues, spending commitments and project execution will matter to creditors already demanding higher returns from less-established infrastructure borrowers. Dealers expect about $25 billion of U.S. high-grade issuance in the coming week, giving the primary market another test after Bank of America's successful sale.

Treasury's October 21 20-year reopening and October 22 five-year TIPS auction arrive before the November 4 refunding decision. Bill auctions continue alongside the rising near-term supply burden. After Friday's broad questionnaire, the key outstanding supply question is whether Treasury changes the long-end mix at the refunding or leaves that adjustment for a later quarter, while inflation-linked demand faces renewed oil-price pressure.

China's Monday GDP and activity releases will show whether industrial strength is reaching domestic demand. Bloomberg's economist survey expects Q3 growth of 4.4% year on year after 4.3%, below the 4.5%-5% annual target range. September industrial output is expected to rise 5.4% after 5.2%, but retail sales only 0.5% after 0.4%; fixed-asset investment is expected to fall 7.3% over the first nine months. The Financial Street Forum starts Monday, offering a current venue for policy signals as investors assess the effect of recent fiscal and funding support.

Britain's Tuesday labor data and Wednesday inflation release will help resolve the disagreement over urgency before the November 5 BOE decision. Economists expect September annual inflation of 3.4%, up from 3.1%, while Bloomberg Economics expects unemployment of 5% in the three months to August after 4.9%. Japan's Friday CPI is expected to show headline and ex-fresh-food inflation at 2.1%, and inflation excluding fresh food and energy at 2.3%. Those observations will put current measured prices beside Ueda's stronger language about underlying inflation.

Indonesia's Wednesday decision carries the immediate currency-confidence test created by MSCI's proposal. South Africa's inflation figures and medium-term budget the same day will show whether the fiscal and monetary discipline cited by Governor Lesetja Kganyago remains on course. France's Friday Moody's review now approaches amid both budget negotiations and the weekend unrest. Brazil's mid-month inflation release precedes the October 25 runoff, with private-credit distress making the eventual fiscal program more consequential than campaign promises alone.

Energy remains an independent risk across those decisions. In early Monday Asian trading, before 07:00 Taipei, Brent slipped after Friday's surge and U.S. equity futures recovered modestly. Zelenskyy's weekend offer to stop attacking Russian refineries in exchange for additional Patriot missiles introduced another conditional diplomatic step, while disruptions from the Strait of Hormuz to the Black Sea persisted. Whether fuel supply improves and whether AI companies can convert commitments into operating revenue remain separate determinants of how far the week's recovery in government bonds can extend.

overall_summary.headline: Short Treasuries rally, but oil and supply disappointment lift long yields
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries ended Friday divided by maturity: the 2-year yield fell 2.99 basis points to 4.7083%, while the 10-year rose 1.48 basis points to 5.0728%. Renewed technology selling supported shorter debt, but Brent's 3.72% rise to $109.86 and disappointment with Treasury's dealer questionnaire weighed on the long end. The survey offered no explicit signal of smaller long-maturity auctions ahead of the November 4 refunding. The 2s10s curve steepened 4.47 basis points to 36.45.

Inflation compensation explained the rise in the nominal 10-year yield: the breakeven increased 2.11 basis points to 2.3508%, while the real yield fell 0.63 basis point to 2.722%. Long bonds still retained substantial weekly gains. Kevin Warsh's remarks reduced expectations for an October Fed increase without ruling out further tightening, while September import prices and industrial production both exceeded expectations.

The Nasdaq 100 lost 2.50% as AI financing concerns moved beyond falling asset prices into new borrowing terms. A $5 billion leveraged-loan sale for Volta Infrastructure required sweeter terms and a yield above the 11% initially discussed. Credit spreads widened modestly in U.S. investment grade and noticeably in high yield and hard-currency emerging markets. Yet Bank of America enlarged its offering to $8 billion, contrasting with postponed mortgage securitizations and showing that established borrowers retained access as other issuers changed financing plans.
